questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before turning on your engine.
While backing out of your driveway.
When approaching speeds of 55 mph.
When completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before turning on your engine.
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, adjust all mirrors so you can see without leaning forward or backward. Check all equipment before starting your engine.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.
Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.
Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Remove your foot from the accelerator and keep both hands on the wheel. Steer parallel to the road and slow down. Ease back onto the road with a small turn when it is safe. Check for traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear. Never rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross, as it is unlikely that a train will be coming.
Dangerous.
Safe locations to park a car.
A place where it is required to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Never cross until you know it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
The road ahead winds a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Reduce your speed, avoid sudden braking or direction changes, and keep more distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: When a drawbridge signal is red, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Quickly speed up.
Proceed with caution.
Stop only if you see a boat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red drawbridge signal means come to a complete stop at the marked line. The bridge is open and no vehicles or pedestrians may cross.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing tracks. Obey all signs and signals. Trains, cars, and bicycles share the road.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Driving with your headlights out of alignment because one side of your car is higher than the other.
Damaging a tire from drifting onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning, if the shoulder has water on it.
Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto a low shoulder, do not slam on the brakes or turn sharply. This could cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not pay attention to how many tracks there are to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look both ways, listen for trains, slow down, and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles using the tracks.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait until the arm is gone.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when you think most children have left the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait until the arm is gone.
questions.explanation: You must stop your vehicle completely when a school bus has its stop arm out. Do not move until the stop arm goes back in.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the side with the broken line.
You can pass from the side with the solid line.
No one can pass in either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass from that side. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass from that side.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turns allowed.
U-turns are allowed.
Road curves ahead.
Sharp left turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means that action is not allowed. This sign means you cannot make U-turns in this area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are most slippery right when rain starts.
Wet roads can cause your tires to lose grip.
Leave more space between you and other cars before stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerous. They are most slippery when rain first starts. Your tires can lose grip, which can cause skidding. You need more distance to stop on wet pavement.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
A T intersection is ahead.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on a bridge over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads with a barrier between them.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A broken white line means you can cross it to pass, as long as it is safe.

questions.question: When you drive faster:

options.text: You see more of the road.
You see less of the road.
You can see cross traffic better.
Your vision does not change.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see less of the road.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. At high speeds, you must pay extra attention to hazards around you.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, even without a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: Before you pass another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before you change lanes.
At any time.
After you change lanes.
Early enough so others know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early before you pass so other drivers have time to see your signal and react.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs mean?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light ahead is red.
The traffic light ahead is broken.
The traffic light ahead is green.
There is a traffic light ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic light ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body must have time to break down alcohol to lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so badly that they look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so badly that they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear drunk. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to fix drowsiness.

questions.question: What should you do if you see water covering the road?

options.text: Drive until you think the water is too deep.
Drive through, since the water is probably not too deep.
Turn around and find another route.
Walk into the water to check how deep it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. You cannot tell how deep the water is or how fast it is moving. Your car could be swept away.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mark dangerous intersections. Stop just like you would at a stop sign.

questions.question: What lights must you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: What happens if a bicycle rider breaks traffic laws?

options.text: They are right because cyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
They can get a ticket.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicycle riders have the same rights and duties as drivers. They can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop because the light will turn red soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and watch for traffic from both sides.

questions.question: What should you do at a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a red light. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if no sign forbids it.
